summary: Shoshone County, Idaho pole lookout about 2 miles northwest of Avery, built about 1939 and destroyed in 1956; a 1925 lookout report may predate it.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1956; no source describes what remains

events.note: Forest lookout at Avery reported a lightning-caused fire near the Bullion mine, per a Morning Oregonian report quoted by Forest Lookouts
About 1939 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab

evidence.supports: patrol lookout on Trego Point 1.5 miles northwest
evidence.quote: There was also a patrol lookout atop Trego Point 1.5 miles northwest.

evidence.supports: forest lookout at Avery reported lightning-caused fire near Bullion mine
evidence.quote: The forest lookout at Avery, 30 miles south of Wallace, reported that lightning caused a fire in the forest near Bullion mine.

evidence.supports: storm cut off wire communication to the district
evidence.quote: Wire communication to the district was cut off later by the storm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 25, 1925 newspaper report, quoted by Forest Lookouts, mentions a forest lookout at Avery before the about-1939 tower. The listings do not say whether it was the same structure, so the story does not connect them.

notes_for_editor: Build (about 1939) and destruction (1956) agree across all three listings. The 1925 report of a forest lookout at Avery is unresolved: it may refer to an earlier lookout or to the later tower's site. The 1925 item is a newspaper report as quoted on Forest Lookouts; the Morning Oregonian itself was not read. The c.1939 and 1956 dates cite Kresek, not read directly. No staffing, access or site-today sources found beyond the drive-up tag.
